terra.problem: The explanation says a prophet speaks for God, a Bible fact outside this passage, without a reference.
The name-tag line is generic and doesn't land as a joke or add much personality.
It assigns Gedaliah the unmarked intention of calming the room before anyone has time to panic. The text doesn't say that.
It equates the Chaldeans with Babylon's army. The passage doesn't define all Chaldeans as the army.
The passage gives fear as the reason for fleeing, but it doesn't establish that nobody followed anyone.
The release happens in the thirty-seventh year of Jehoiachin's exile, not necessarily after thirty-seven completed years in prison.
The line about Papa knowing doors that open after a long wait alludes to his backstory without identifying the drawer.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the verse and its meaning, with little of Papa's voice.
The explanation restates the same fact several times without adding much of Papa's personality.

The passage places the release in the thirty-seventh year of exile, not after a stated thirty-seven-year wait. It also doesn't say how long Jehoiachin lived afterward, so the portion can't be said to have lasted more than twelve months.
